title: Kasiri Ruza
dek: A craftswoman who investigates the Gate, seeks supplies and partnerships for her workshop, and argues that Pristinia deserves support after sheltering adventurers.

facts.Recorded at: The Gate and road to Pristinia

sources: Gate chronicle · selected arrival and welcome scenes; January 2024–September 2026 posting records
Supplied character deep dives · 11 October 2026; interpretation checked against selected primary scenes where available.
body:
Kasiri’s curiosity at the Gate and her work as a craftswoman share a practical question: what can be learned and made useful here? Her supplied shop account adds a second problem. Skill alone cannot sustain a workshop without materials, hunters, customers and reliable cooperation.

A capable maker in an empty shop

The supplied character dossier describes Kasiri as a junior partner in a Pristinian shop associated with Olokun, crediting Wren with the storefront’s construction. In its account, Kasiri sits in a dusty, mostly empty shop and identifies shortages of materials, organization and interest alongside competition. She has made a suit of plate armor to prove she can, yet that achievement has not produced a functioning supply network. The workshop’s exact name, ownership arrangement and subsequent recovery remain unconfirmed by these supplied materials.

Making something requires other people

Kasiri’s shop account distinguishes having metal and relics from having every ingredient a commission needs. Plant matter and hunted monster components can still be missing. She is candid about not yet mastering attunement-related craft and about the items she cannot make. These are limits described at that point in her development, rather than a permanent ceiling on her abilities. She seeks cooperation instead of promising work she cannot deliver.

Severina brings the field to the workshop

The dossier describes Severina as a practical counterpart: she can supply hunted components and bring demand for equipment, while Kasiri can turn those materials into durable tools. Kasiri brightens when a partnership becomes possible, jokes about unsuitable wooden or metal shoes and improvises seating when the shop has none. Her precision has warmth and embarrassment alongside it. The account supports a working relationship; it does not establish a completed contract or every proposed commission.

What Pristinia paid to shelter adventurers

In the Public Square, Kasiri tells a newcomer about flaming projectiles, damaged buildings, displaced families and Melian’s capture during the Rahu siege. She connects that memory to peace and rebuilding. When asked to condemn the Rahu collectively, she distinguishes harmful actions from a judgment against every individual. Her knowledge is informed and limited; her account is testimony, rather than a claim to know every combatant’s motives.

Primary scene: 1, 2, 3. Dates refer to Discord posts.

Craft as repayment

The supplied dossier describes Kasiri’s wish to give Pristinia more than the usual local fee: in her view, the town paid dearly to shelter adventurers when it could have blamed them. That is her assessment of a civic debt. It gives her work a purpose beyond selling equipment, while leaving the amount and completion of any additional contribution unresolved.

What remains unresolved

The supplied shop account has no message-level references or established scene date, so its details retain that provenance. Kasiri’s later mastery, the shop’s fate and the exact meaning of her occasional description of herself as a watcher remain open. Her work and her civic testimony both favor a similar discipline: use what is known, acknowledge what is missing and make cooperation possible.

Curiosity at the Gate

Kasiri approaches the activating Gate with Krasteline, eager to understand its workings. Their examination identifies ancient teleportation magic, but no discernible internal power source. Its unfamiliar runes and numerous moving parts defeat a complete reading. This limits what their investigation establishes; it does not prove the Gate has no power source.

Recognition across worlds

Kasiri introduces herself to Fenwick d’Jorasco as an archaeologist and tinkerer formerly associated with Morgrave University in Breland. She reveals a dragonmark and identifies herself with House Medani. Fenwick recognises the name; she recognises House Jorasco. Their shared recognition is an unexpected connection to home.

What remains in front of her

Kasiri tells Fenwick that, as far as she knows, nobody called here has returned. That is her knowledge at the time, not proof of a universal law. She says focusing on what is here helps her cope with missing family and friends.

profile.relationships: Recognizes Fenwick through their shared home-world institutions. The shop dossier names Olokun as a partner, credits Wren’s storefront and describes cooperation with Severina. Her public testimony links Pristinia’s losses to responsibility for rebuilding.
profile.personality: Practical, curious and candid about limits. The supplied shop account portrays her as a maker seeking materials and partnerships rather than overpromising; her siege testimony resists blaming every Rahu individual.
profile.achievements: Investigates the Gate and welcomes Fenwick. The supplied dossier describes plate armor she made to prove her skill, a struggling workshop and attempts to connect crafting with hunters and material supply.
